evidence.note: Built custom per-suite filter.json subsets to run c_testsuite/wacc/gcc_torture independently and get faster, feature-scoped signal instead of only the full 780-suite; used pass counts per suite to gauge state.

For div_neg failure, ran the single test capturing runtime exit code, then dumped emitted asm with -S, diagnosed exact instruction bug (negl zeroing upper 32 bits / missing sign extension) — asm inspection against expected behavior.

Bisected an 'undefined reference to cy' bug via a chain of minimal C repros (swap.c, q.c, r.c..r4.c) narrowing to 'unsigned char' vs 'char' vs 'int', combined with -S asm inspection, pinning it to an off==-1 sentinel collision — bug isolated to a single instruction/branch.
Categorized gcc_torture failures by grouping (grep FAIL | uniq -c, splitting FAIL(compile) vs run), a root-cause triage of failures rather than guess-and-recompile.

Float comparison bug: dumped asm, saw wrong movq vs movsd/comparison handling, fixed, re-ran targeted wacc test confirming return value 1, then full suite — verifying compile + runtime at right granularity.

Range-case (pr34154): minimal reasoning about immediate size and unsigned comparison (ja/jb vs jl/jg), tested single file iteratively, then produced a feature-categorized breakdown of the final 22 remaining failures by root cause.

reasoning: Across the entire arc the agent ran a deliberate, tight verification loop: minimal reproductions for failing constructs, repeated -S assembly inspection against expected instructions, per-feature/per-suite test slices, and verification of both compile success and runtime exit codes — squarely matching the level-8 anchor. It also shows level-10 touches (failure categorization by root cause via grep/uniq, confirming edge semantics like sign extension, truncation, and signed/unsigned comparison, bisecting to a single sentinel-value bug). It stops short of full 10 because the tooling is ad-hoc (temporary filter.json subsets, manual asm reading) rather than reusable auto-diffing/bisecting infrastructure.
